name: Use Alternate Authentication Material
description:
Adversaries may use alternate authentication material, such as password hashes, Kerberos tickets, and application access tokens, in order to move laterally within an environment and bypass normal system access controls. 

Authentication processes generally require a valid identity (e.g., username) along with one or more authentication factors (e.g., password, pin, physical smart card, token generator, etc.). Alternate authentication material is legitimately generated by systems after a user or application successfully authenticates by providing a valid identity and the required authentication factor(s). Alternate authentication material may also be generated during the identity creation process.(Citation: NIST Authentication)(Citation: NIST MFA)

Caching alternate authentication material allows the system to verify an identity has successfully authenticated without asking the user to reenter authentication factor(s). Because the alternate authentication must be maintained by the system—either in memory or on disk—it may be at risk of being stolen through [Credential Access](https://attack.mitre.org/tactics/TA0006) techniques. By stealing alternate authentication material, adversaries are able to bypass system access controls and authenticate to systems without knowing the plaintext password or any additional authentication factors.

telemetry.name: Application Log Content
telemetry.description: Application-emitted audit or operational event content.
telemetry.collection_focus: Select the application event family required by the detection and document its native schema before normalization.

providers.name: Application audit logs
providers.scope: First-party service events and request/result fields; schema is application-specific.

providers.name: OpenTelemetry-compatible log pipelines
providers.scope: Transport and normalization of emitted records; do not create missing audit instrumentation.

configuration: Enable the application audit category or instrument the owned lab application at the authorization/action boundary.
Define a schema with timestamp, service, actor, object, action, result and correlation ID. Export structured records through an authenticated collector.
Redact secrets and personal content, separate audit from debug logs, set retention and verify delivery during rotation/restart.
telemetry.example_note: Project-normalized synthetic JSON, not a native provider log, captured event, attack verdict or validated detection. A parser/adapter is required for a real SIEM. Example names, IPs and values are fictional.
telemetry.limitations: Debug output is not necessarily a durable audit trail. Application developers must emit the relevant event; installing a log pipeline does not make an absent event exist.
telemetry.anomaly_design: Per application, client and route: request rate, rare actions, failure ratios and unusual state transitions. Version changes, retries, health probes and seasonal load need separate baselines.

telemetry.name: Logon Session Creation
telemetry.description: Creation of a logon session with account and logon-type context.
telemetry.collection_focus: Enable Audit Logon and collect successful session creation on the receiving host; join session/logon IDs rather than only account names.

providers.name: Windows Security auditing
providers.scope: Policy-dependent account, object, task and logon records on the host that performs the operation.

configuration: Use a lab-only GPO under Computer Configuration → Windows Settings → Security Settings → Advanced Audit Policy Configuration. Enable the specific subcategory named below.
For object-level auditing, configure a narrow system access control list (SACL) on the test object in addition to policy. Do not audit an entire production directory by default.

Forward Security events from the responsible host or controller; retain subject and target identities, object identifiers, result and original XML. Confirm effective policy with auditpol /get /category:*.
telemetry.example_note: Project-normalized synthetic JSON, not a native provider log, captured event, attack verdict or validated detection. A parser/adapter is required for a real SIEM. Example names, IPs and values are fictional.
telemetry.limitations: A policy checkbox alone does not guarantee an event. Host role, SACL, success/failure selection and audit policy precedence matter. Directory changes may arrive as multiple records.
telemetry.anomaly_design: Per principal, host and object: unusual access/request rates, new principal-object relationships, and changes outside approved administration windows. Control for service accounts and scheduled directory maintenance.

telemetry.name: Process Creation
telemetry.description: Creation of a process with executable, command line, parent and security context.
telemetry.collection_focus: Collect Sysmon ProcessCreate (1); preserve ProcessGuid and parent identifiers. Security 4688 is an alternative with separate audit/command-line settings.

providers.name: Microsoft Sysmon
providers.scope: Windows event-based collection; enable the event types needed below.

providers.name: Linux Audit
providers.scope: Linux alternative for supported system-call and file events; different semantics and fields.

providers.name: Apple Endpoint Security clients
providers.scope: macOS alternative where the subscribed event exists; requires an entitled, approved client, not an iOS collector.

configuration: On a disposable Windows host, review the installed Sysmon schema and current configuration; merge scoped event filters into the existing policy rather than replacing it.
Forward Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational to the lab collector. Preserve event ID, timestamp, computer, process identifiers and the original event.
For Linux or macOS, select the equivalent sensor separately and test its emitted fields; a Windows event ID does not transfer across platforms.

configuration_example.label: Sysmon filter fragment · merge into the reviewed lab configuration
configuration_example.note: This fragment only selects the named process. It is not a complete production policy. Inspect the installed schema with sysmon64 -s; preserve existing rules, then apply the reviewed complete configuration with sysmon64 -c <configuration-file>.

telemetry.example_note: Project-normalized synthetic JSON, not a native provider log, captured event, attack verdict or validated detection. A parser/adapter is required for a real SIEM. Example names, IPs and values are fictional.
telemetry.limitations: Event filtering and sensor versions change coverage. High-volume image-load and process-access collection needs tuning; endpoint events alone do not establish intent.

sources.title: Apple Endpoint Security framework for macOS

telemetry.anomaly_design: Per host role and user: rare process/object combinations, bursts of object access or modification, and ordered parent/action sequences. Compare maintenance windows and signed software rollout activity.

telemetry.name: User Account Authentication
telemetry.description: Authentication attempts and outcomes for a user or workload account.
telemetry.collection_focus: Collect successful and failed sign-ins, authentication method, application and conditional-access context; distinguish account validation from session creation.

providers.name: Microsoft Entra sign-in logs
providers.scope: Interactive, non-interactive and workload sign-in contexts, subject to tenant features and access.

providers.name: Cloud identity service audit
providers.scope: Issuer-side credential and administrative events where the service supports them.

providers.name: Application audit instrumentation
providers.scope: Application-side use of identities and sessions; design fields without raw tokens.

configuration: Enable/export the required identity sign-in and audit categories from the lab tenant to a protected destination. Document license, role and retention requirements.
Correlate issuance or administrative changes with later sign-ins using non-secret credential IDs, application IDs, user IDs and correlation IDs.
Exclude passwords, bearer tokens, cookies and private keys. Record success, failure, authentication context and application result separately.
telemetry.example_note: Project-normalized synthetic JSON, not a native provider log, captured event, attack verdict or validated detection. A parser/adapter is required for a real SIEM. Example names, IPs and values are fictional.
telemetry.limitations: A token creation record is not evidence of token use; a sign-in is not a complete record of every resource access. Some provider-side data is unavailable to the customer.
telemetry.anomaly_design: Per identity and application: first-seen clients/resources, changes in authentication failures and session patterns, and unusual permission changes. Separate automation, travel, shared egress and identity-provider policy changes.

telemetry.name: User Account Metadata
telemetry.description: Account inventory and attributes at a point in time.
telemetry.collection_focus: Export an authorized directory/account inventory with stable IDs, roles, enabled state and collection time; compare snapshots without exposing credentials.

providers.name: osquery
providers.scope: Scheduled host-state queries; supported tables and privileges vary by OS. Select a table that actually exposes the required object.

providers.name: Linux Audit plus inventory snapshots
providers.scope: Events explain changes; snapshots describe state at collection time.

configuration: Define the inventory query, allowed host set, interval and least-privileged reader. Store a stable asset ID, observation time and collector version.
Keep successive snapshots and calculate additions, removals and changed attributes. Pair state changes with audit events when available.
Export collector health and missed-poll counts so a missing snapshot is not misclassified as a missing asset.
telemetry.example_note: Project-normalized synthetic JSON, not a native provider log, captured event, attack verdict or validated detection. A parser/adapter is required for a real SIEM. Example names, IPs and values are fictional.
telemetry.limitations: Snapshots miss short-lived objects and do not identify who caused a change. A generic inventory agent is not guaranteed to expose firmware or kernel-level details.
telemetry.anomaly_design: Compare authorized state snapshots: first-seen drivers/services/modules, unexpected configuration drift and integrity changes. Record collection cadence; absence in a sample is not evidence of deletion.

strategies.name: Behavioral Detection Strategy for Use Alternate Authentication Material (T1550)

analytics.name: Analytic 0954
analytics.guidance: Use of stolen Kerberos tickets or token impersonation resulting in logon sessions from accounts without expected interactive logon events.

tuning.description: Allows tuning of how far apart related logon and process events can be correlated
Customize for high-value or service accounts with restricted access policies

analytics.name: Analytic 0955
analytics.guidance: Access tokens or SSH keys used without corresponding login shell or PAM module activity, particularly for remote execution.

tuning.description: Tune for approved jump boxes or bastion hosts
Filter on use of password vs publickey methods for better coverage

log_sources.name: auditd:SYSCALL
log_sources.channel: execution of ssh, scp, or sftp using previously unseen credentials or keys

log_sources.name: NSM:Connections
log_sources.channel: Accepted publickey for user from unusual IP or without tty

analytics.name: Analytic 0956
analytics.guidance: Token replay or impersonation in federated logins without interactive browser session or MFA prompts.

tuning.description: Customize for accounts where MFA must always precede token issuance
Threshold for number of times a refresh token is reused without re-auth

log_sources.name: m365:unified
log_sources.channel: login using refresh_token with no preceding authentication context

analytics.name: Analytic 0957
analytics.guidance: Unusual reuse of OAuth access tokens from different geographic regions, without full login events.

tuning.description: Minimum distance between token reuse events to trigger detection

analytics.name: Analytic 0958
analytics.guidance: Container process uses mounted cloud credentials or token cache to authenticate without known orchestration.

tuning.description: Restrict to prod workloads or certain namespaces
Path used to mount sensitive tokens (e.g., /.aws/credentials)

log_sources.name: docker:runtime
log_sources.channel: execution of cloud CLI tool (e.g., aws, az) inside container

analytics.name: Analytic 0959
analytics.guidance: Access token reuse to connect to SharePoint or Outlook APIs without interactive user context.

tuning.description: Tune to detect access from CLI agents or scripts rather than interactive browsers

analytics.name: Analytic 0960
analytics.guidance: Use of instance metadata tokens across instances or misuse of short-lived tokens issued for different roles.

tuning.description: Time window where token reuse is suspicious
Enable if tokens for RoleA are used in resources only RoleB should access

software.name: FoggyWeb
software.description: [FoggyWeb](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S0661) can allow abuse of a compromised AD FS server's SAML token.(Citation: MSTIC FoggyWeb September 2021)

references.description: Ramin Nafisi. (2021, September 27). FoggyWeb: Targeted NOBELIUM malware leads to persistent backdoor. Retrieved October 4, 2021.

mitigations.name: Application Developer Guidance
mitigations.description: Consider implementing token binding strategies, such as Azure AD token protection or OAuth Proof of Possession, that cryptographically bind a token to a secret. This may prevent the token from being used without knowledge of the secret or possession of the device the token is tied to.(Citation: Microsoft Token Protection 2023)(Citation: Okta DPoP 2023)

references.description: Microsoft. (2023, October 23). Conditional Access: Token protection (preview). Retrieved January 2, 2024.
Venkat Viswanathan. (2023, June 13). A leap forward in token security: Okta adds support for DPoP. Retrieved January 2, 2024.

mitigations.name: Active Directory Configuration
mitigations.description: Configure Active Directory to prevent use of certain techniques; use SID Filtering, etc.

mitigations.name: User Account Management
mitigations.description: Enforce the principle of least-privilege. Do not allow a domain user to be in the local administrator group on multiple systems.

mitigations.name: Privileged Account Management
mitigations.description: Limit credential overlap across systems to prevent the damage of credential compromise and reduce the adversary's ability to perform Lateral Movement between systems.

mitigations.name: Password Policies
mitigations.description: Set and enforce secure password policies for accounts.

mitigations.name: Account Use Policies
mitigations.description: Where possible, consider restricting the use of authentication material outside of expected contexts.

mitigations.name: Audit
mitigations.description: Perform audits or scans of systems, permissions, insecure software, insecure configurations, etc. to identify potential weaknesses.

simulation.prerequisites: Use disposable lab hosts and test accounts, explicit target allowlists, a clean snapshot, bounded egress and a restore plan. Review every candidate and dependency before any execution.
